sub_questions: What are the measured attrition rates of content creators over time — what share stop creating, and how soon after starting?
What are the measured survival rates of channels/accounts (as distinct from persons) over time — cohort persistence, dormancy, upload-cessation curves?
What is the income distribution across creators — specifically the median versus the mean, and the shape/skew of the distribution (top-decile share, Gini, share earning zero)?
What share of creators earns a living wage, and how is that threshold operationally defined in each study (and in each country's terms)?
How long does it take from starting to first meaningful income — time to monetization eligibility, time to first payout, time to a defined income floor?
What reasons do creators themselves give for quitting, as documented in surveys or exit studies, and with what instrument and sample?
Which of the above findings rest on US/Western samples only, and therefore may not generalize to Southeast Asia?
What quantitative evidence, if any, exists specifically for Southeast Asian creator populations (Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, and the rest of ASEAN)?
How do measured platform telemetry findings differ from self-reported survey findings on the same quantities, and by how much?

entities.name: content creators (persons)
entities.scope_note: Broad reading: video creators, livestreamers, short-form creators, writers/newsletter authors, podcasters, influencers, and UGC/affiliate creators. NOT narrowed to full-time professionals.

entities.name: channels / accounts (as a unit of analysis distinct from persons)
entities.scope_note: Channel-level survival has a different denominator from person-level attrition. Both must be reported and the difference stated.

entities.name: United States / Western economies
required_fields: which findings are drawn from these samples

entities.name: Southeast Asia
entities.scope_note: Full ASEAN scope: Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, Brunei, Timor-Leste. Must not be collapsed to a single country.

entities.name: meaningful income
required_fields: operational definition per study — monetization eligibility, first payout, or an income floor

required_formats: Every reported figure must carry four metadata fields: sample size, year, platform, and country
Tabular presentation of figures (the four-field metadata requirement is table-shaped; prose alone cannot carry it legibly)
Explicit per-finding geographic-scope flag marking US/Western-only results
Median AND mean reported side by side wherever income is discussed
required_section_headings: ## 1. Attrition and Survival Rates of Creators and Channels
## 2. Income Distribution Across Creators: Median vs Mean and the Living-Wage Share
## 3. Time from Starting to First Meaningful Income
## 4. Documented Reasons Creators Give for Quitting
## 5. Geographic Scope: Which Findings Are US/Western-Only, and What Is Known for Southeast Asia
time_horizons: no forward horizon requested — the query is retrospective

evidence recency window: 2018-2026 is load-bearing (YouTube's 2018 Partner Program threshold change and TikTok's 2023 Creator Rewards change break comparability with earlier cohorts); pre-2018 figures usable only when explicitly period-labelled
scope_conditions: QUANTITATIVE ONLY — 'Cover only measurable findings'. Qualitative theorizing, opinion, and unquantified commentary are out of scope except as labelled context for a number.

Content creation framed AS AN OCCUPATION — income-generating activity. Cover BOTH readings: full-time professional creators AND part-time/side-income creators seeking earnings. Do not silently narrow to full-time.
Unit-of-analysis discipline: creator-level (person) and channel-level (account) findings are distinct and must not be conflated.
Any figure lacking one of the four required metadata fields (sample size, year, platform, country) must be explicitly annotated as incomplete rather than presented as if complete.
Multi-platform coverage required — do not let YouTube stand in for 'creators' generally.

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing order: academic APIs first (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv cs.CY/econ.GN, SSRN, NBER) for platform-labour and creator-economy panel studies — this literature is real and citation-ranked, and web search returns mostly vendor marketing in its place. Then platform-disclosed and administrative data (YouTube/TikTok transparency and payout disclosures, Patreon/Substack public payout data, national statistical agencies, tax-authority self-employment data). Then gray literature for Southeast Asia specifically: ADB, World Bank, ILO, national statistics offices (BPS Indonesia, PSA Philippines, NSO Thailand), and regional platform reports — SEA quantitative evidence is thin on the clear web and lives here. Vendor surveys (Influencer Marketing Hub, NeoReach, Linktree, Adobe, Kajabi) MAY be cited but MUST be labelled as self-selected vendor surveys with sample size stated, and must never outrank telemetry or peer-reviewed panel data on the same quantity. Evidence norms for this topic: measured platform telemetry and administrative records > peer-reviewed longitudinal panels > cross-sectional academic surveys > self-selected vendor surveys > press-cited round numbers with no traceable methodology (exclude these last entirely). Survivorship bias is the dominant failure mode — any sample recruited from active creators systematically overstates income and understates attrition, and this must be flagged wherever it applies. Recency window: 2018-2026, with 2021-2026 preferred; monetization-threshold changes make older cohorts non-comparable.

rationale.register: The query says 'Cover only measurable findings' and 'Report every figure with sample size, year, platform, and country' — explicitly enumerative and coverage-shaped. No verdict, recommendation, or comparative judgement is requested. Strong survey signal.
rationale.inference_depth: Two of the required deliverables likely have no direct answer on the clear web: the living-wage share (requires combining an income distribution with a country-specific threshold) and Southeast Asian creator statistics (gray literature, national statistics offices, non-English sources). Inference over absences — stating clearly which figures do not exist — is part of the deliverable.
rationale.tier: Multi-domain quantitative synthesis across a contested literature where telemetry and survey evidence systematically disagree, plus an explicit transferability assessment. Requires adversarial review to avoid laundering vendor survey numbers as measurements.
rationale.response_format: Coverage across four measurable domains plus a geographic audit, with a four-field metadata requirement per figure. Scannability and completeness matter more than argumentative density — but the survivorship-bias and survey-vs-telemetry tensions still need adversarial depth, hence full tier with structured format.
